Imagine falling asleep at your desk... and your boss being impressed.
It's called inemuri, which means sleeping while present.
Japanese workers are some of the most sleep-deprived people on the planet.
So when someone dozes off at work, people often think: wow, he must be working really hard.
You have to stay sitting up, like you could jump back into the meeting at any second.
And it helps to be important.
A boss napping in a meeting looks dedicated.
A new employee doing the same thing? Not so much.
So next time you fall asleep in class... just tell your teacher you're practicing inemuri.
